title: Restriction commutes with gate evaluation
statement:
Fix $n$ variables and let $C_1,\dots,C_k$ be a finite list of Boolean circuits on them, let $\rho$ be a restriction, and let $b$ be a Boolean flag. For a Boolean function $f$ write $f_\rho$ for its restriction by $\rho$, the function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$. Form the circuit node with children $C_1,\dots,C_k$, read as an AND gate when $b$ is true and as an OR gate when $b$ is false, and let $g$ be its evaluation. Then the restriction of the gate's evaluation agrees, as a Boolean function, with the gate applied to the restricted evaluations of the children: for every assignment $x$,
\[
g_\rho(x) =
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k} (C_i)_\rho(x) & \text{if } b = \mathrm{true},\\[1ex]
\displaystyle\bigvee_{i=1}^{k} (C_i)_\rho(x) & \text{if } b = \mathrm{false},
\end{cases}
\]
where $(C_i)_\rho$ denotes the restriction by $\rho$ of the evaluation of $C_i$, an empty conjunction is $\mathrm{true}$, and an empty disjunction is $\mathrm{false}$.
hypotheses_covered: a Boolean flag isAnd selecting AND vs OR
a finite list cs of child circuits
empty conjunction unit is true, empty disjunction unit is false
replaced:
The restriction of the evaluation of a node circuit equals the conjunction or disjunction,
according to $\mathit{isAnd}$, of the restricted evaluations of its children. That is,
$\mathrm{restrictFn}\,(\mathrm{eval}\,(\mathrm{node}\,\mathit{isAnd}\,cs))\,\rho$ sends $x$
to the fold-$\mathrm{and}$ over $cs$ of $\mathrm{restrictFn}\,c.\mathrm{eval}\,\rho\,x$ when
$\mathit{isAnd}$ is true, and to the corresponding fold-$\mathrm{or}$ otherwise.
